question.instructions: Does this change add an unsafe escape hatch: a null value or null check, a throw, an asInstanceOf or isInstanceOf, an overridden finalize, or NonEmptyList.fromListUnsafe?

criteria.true: val x: String = null; throw new IllegalStateException(...); value.asInstanceOf[Order]; if x.isInstanceOf[Foo]; override def finalize(); NonEmptyList.fromListUnsafe(xs)
criteria.false: Option/Either/IO.raiseError instead of null or throw; a pattern match (case o: Order =>); NonEmptyList.fromList(xs) returning Option; the words only in a string or identifier

question.instructions: Does this change paper over a dynamic value: getOrElse("") on an optional value, a collect { case s: String => s } that silently drops values of other types, or repeated .toUnit(...) calls extracting units from a duration?

criteria.true: name.getOrElse(""); values.collect { case s: String => s }; d.toUnit(HOURS) at several call sites
criteria.false: absence kept as Option; an explicit decode that reports the mismatch; a refined duration type with inHours/inMinutes accessors

question.instructions: Does this change check a domain invariant unsafely instead of with a refined type: a require(...), .applyUnsafe, .refineUnsafe, .assume on a string literal, or a domain id declared as a bare alias of a primitive (type UserId = UUID)?

criteria.true: require(amount > 0); Port.applyUnsafe(n); s.refineUnsafe[Email]; "abc".assume[Slug]; type OrderId = UUID
criteria.false: an Iron refined type built with its constructor for literals or .option/.either at a boundary; object OrderId extends RefinedSubtype[UUID, Pure]

question.instructions: Does this change use imperative or pre-Scala-3 constructs: a var, a return statement, a while loop, or a sealed trait with case classes where a Scala 3 enum would do?

criteria.true: var total = 0; return None inside a method; while i < n do ...; sealed trait Status with case objects Active/Closed
criteria.false: vals with fold/traverse/recursion; an expression as the method result; enum Status { case Active, Closed }; a sealed trait used as an empty marker or phantom type

question.instructions: Does this change add a modifier or annotation the project forbids: final on a case class, class or def, a qualified private[pkg]/protected[pkg], a .Default value on a companion, or a @nowarn annotation?

criteria.true: final case class Order(...); final class Service; final def run; private[billing] def helper; val Default = Settings(...) in a companion; @nowarn("msg=unused")
criteria.false: plain case class, class and def; plain private; values passed explicitly at the call site; the underlying warning fixed

question.instructions: Does this change break the project's Scala 3 syntax style: a braced lambda (.map { x => ...}), a parenthesised braced if, a code comment, an import of cats.syntax.all.*, or positional tuple access (._1, ._2)?

criteria.true: xs.map { x => f(x) }; if (ok) { a } else { b }; // explain; import cats.syntax.all.*; pair._1
criteria.false: xs.map: x => f(x); if ok then a else b; no comments (scala-cli //> directives are fine); import cats.syntax.traverse.*; val (left, right) = pair

question.instructions: Does this change add a type ascription that inference already handles: on a private or protected val, the return type of a private or protected def, or a local val/var/def inside a method?

criteria.true: private val limit: Int = 10; private def total(xs: List[Money]): Money = ...; inside a method val count: Int = xs.size
criteria.false: ascriptions on public API members; a recursive def that needs its return type; private val limit = 10

question.instructions: Does this change misuse effects: reading the clock directly (Instant.now, System.currentTimeMillis), unsafeRun* outside the app entry point, importing cats.effect.unsafe.implicits.global, an IO-level recover inside a cats-mtl Handle.allow scope, an unbounded parEvalMapUnbounded, or Session.single in production code?

criteria.true: Instant.now(); io.unsafeRunSync(); import cats.effect.unsafe.implicits.global; .recover inside Handle.allow; stream.parEvalMapUnbounded(f); Session.single(...) outside tests
criteria.false: Clock[F].realTimeInstant; returning IO and letting IOApp run it; recovery outside the allow scope; parEvalMap(8)(f); Session.pooled

question.instructions: Does this change add a duplication smell: a Utils object or file, the same numeric literal repeated instead of a named constant, an import block duplicated from another file, or foldLeft(empty)(_ |+| _) instead of combineAll?

criteria.true: object StringUtils; 86400 written three times; the same 6-line import block pasted into a new file; xs.foldLeft(Monoid.empty)(_ |+| _)
criteria.false: a domain-named module; a named constant; xs.combineAll

question.instructions: Does this Laminar frontend change misuse the reactive model: js.JSON.stringify on an Airstream or DOM value, raw js.timers.setTimeout, .now() inside a signal combinator, child <-- signal.map { case ... } on an ADT, currentPageSignal.map to render pages, or an import from the server-side api package?

criteria.true: js.JSON.stringify(signal); js.timers.setTimeout(500)(...); a.signal.map(x => b.now() + x); child <-- page.map { case Home => ...; case Map => ... }; router.currentPageSignal.map(render); import com.acme.api.OrderDto
criteria.false: EventStream.delay / periodic; withCurrentValueOf or sample; splitMatchOne with handleCase; SplitRender; DTOs from shared/model
